text: Project 3 is a payments platform's fraud detector: every transaction needs a fraud score back before it's approved — a latency budget measured in hundreds of milliseconds. There's no overnight batch job that can help here.

Assume a mid-size processor: roughly two thousand transactions a second at peak, a 300 millisecond scoring budget, ninety days of retained raw events. These numbers alone rule out entire design classes before any tool gets picked.

A fraud detector has no batch layer to begin with — every transaction is scored once, live, by one pipeline. If the scoring logic changes, replay historical transactions through the updated pipeline to backtest it.

The serving layer returning approve or flag has to answer inside the latency budget, every time, under peak load. A slow serving layer here is a fraud detector that approves what it should have flagged.
The scenario, the numbers, and the architecture fit are set. Next up: streaming ingestion and the real-time feature computation the scoring model runs on.
